plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds erupt into slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue blossoms. The flowers hum with bees and scent the warm air across the fields of Provence.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late June through August, with peak bloom in early to mid July
plants.funFact: Lavender belongs to the mint family. Its name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Nymphaea alba
plants.description: Star-shaped white blooms with golden centers float on still ponds and lakes. They sit on broad, round, glossy green pads and open wide on sunny mornings.
plants.location: Lakes and slow waters across Europe, including the United Kingdom
plants.funFact: The flowers open in the morning and close in the afternoon. After pollination, the stalk coils and pulls the developing fruit underwater.

plants.name: Agapanthus praecox
plants.description: Tall, bare stems carry round clusters of trumpet-shaped blue flowers above arching, strap-like leaves. They are a vivid sight in summer gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer in the Northern Hemisphere, around June to August. In its native South Africa it flowers in the southern summer, from about November to February.
plants.location: Gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, including the Mediterranean and the southern United States
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Greek words 'agape' (love) and 'anthos' (flower), so it means 'flower of love'.
